module_title: Peninsular Rivers - Origins, Tributaries, and Inland Drainage
introduction: At this level, we memorize the specific origin points of major rivers, their important tributaries, and explore exceptions like the perennial nature of the Cauvery and the inland drainage of the Luni.

core_concepts.title: Points of Origin
core_concepts.description: Godavari: Trimbakeshwar (Nashik, Maharashtra). Krishna: Mahabaleshwar (Maharashtra). Narmada: Amarkantak (Madhya Pradesh). Tapi: Multai (Betul, MP). Mahanadi: Sihawa (Chhattisgarh). Cauvery: Brahmagiri Hills (Karnataka).

core_concepts.title: Cauvery River: The Perennial Exception
core_concepts.description: While peninsular rivers dry up in summer, the Cauvery is almost perennial. Why? Its upper catchment area receives rainfall from the 'South-West Monsoon' (summer), while the lower catchment receives rainfall from the 'Retreating/North-East Monsoon' (winter).

core_concepts.title: The Luni River
core_concepts.description: Originates in the Aravallis (Pushkar, Rajasthan). It is an 'Inland Drainage' river, meaning it never reaches the ocean. It loses its way and disappears into the salty marshes of the 'Rann of Kutch' in Gujarat.

core_concepts.title: Tributaries of Krishna and Mahanadi
core_concepts.description: Krishna's tributaries: Tungabhadra, Bhima, Musi (Hyderabad sits on the banks of Musi). Mahanadi's tributaries: Seonath, Hasdeo, Ong, Tel.

important_entities.name: Hirakud Dam
important_entities.significance: Built across the Mahanadi in Odisha, the Hirakud Dam is the longest earthen dam in the world.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: Mahi River and the Tropic of Cancer
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: The Mahi river (west-flowing) has a unique geographical distinction: it cuts across the 'Tropic of Cancer' TWICE. This is a highly tested trivia fact.

Rivers originate from the Amarkantak plateau and flow in different directions: Narmada flows West, Son flows North (to join the Ganga), and Mahanadi flows East. This outward flow from a central peak is called 'Radial Drainage'.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Penganga, Indravati, Wainganga, Wardha. These are the major left-bank tributaries of the Godavari.

exam_strategy_tips: Direct matching questions (River -> Origin Point) are incredibly common. Rote memorize pairs like Krishna-Mahabaleshwar and Godavari-Trimbakeshwar.
If a question asks 'Which river does not join the sea?', the answer is almost always the Luni.
